outcome.answer: For a review centered on programmable scripts as the structure for assistant reasoning and tool execution, “Code as Agent Harness” is the closest match: it surveys code as the substrate connecting reasoning, planning, memory, tool use, feedback, execution, and multi-agent coordination, and discusses applications and open engineering challenges [2]. “The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling” is narrower and empirically compares script-based programmatic tool calling with native JSON calls [1]. Related perspectives cover reusable procedural skills [3], compiling repeated procedures into validated tools [8], and encoding operating procedures as execution graphs [9].
